decoded.meaning: SETTINGS{NAME "addr" NAME "127.0.0.1", NAME "port" VALUE u16=8080} — RFC-0014 §2 `bad-payload-type`: a TLV that is neither SPEC nor NAME, written to /net/<module>/conn; refused `tr::schema::type_mismatch` (0x0030), and NOT assigned
decoded.note: These bytes are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the `config` child of `conn/create-via-spec` — the same connection config with its SPEC envelope stripped off. That is the point: the endpoint selects the operation by the written TLV's TYPE, not by what the payload contains, so a well-formed config that names no operation is refused rather than guessed at. The endpoint is write-only and valueless (RFC-0014 §2): it never falls through to an ordinary assign, so nothing is stored and nothing propagates to subscribers.
